# Page 20^page=20
20Avalanche Photodiode (APD) • P-i-N junction • Bias: below but close to breakdown • Analog output proportional to incoming light • Internal multiplication (gain: M ≈ 100) Basic structure: - absorption region = separate photo-generated holes and electrons - multiplication region = high electric field to provide internal photo-current gain by impact ionization absorption region avalanche region

# Page 21^page=21
21Single-Photon Avalanche-Diode (SPAD) • P-N junction • Bias: well ABOVE breakdown • digital output • single photon sensitivity • no read-out noise • output: >10 mA current for every photon solid-state device: can be integrated together with electronics (counter & TDC) p+n+ ph I V VBD Va = VBD+VEX hν “avalanche” “quench” “reset”

# Page 22^page=22
22Silicon Photo-Multipliers Hundreds / thousands SPADs + quenching resistance in parallel  Single photon sensitivity  Photon number resolving capability  Large active area

# Page 23^page=23
23Light Dependent Resistor (LDR) In the dark  R very high (up to 1MΩ) Exposed to light  R drops dramatically (few ohms) Working principle: Photons excite electrons from the valence band to the conduction band  more free electrons in the material  lower resistance But… - low sensitivity - non-linear characteristic - sensitive to temperature changes

# Page 24^page=24
24Typical application WITHOUT LIGHT High LDR VBE < 0.7  BJT off  LED off WITH LIGHT Low LDR VBE = 0.7  BJT on  LED on
